column1: # What's coming: the curated source for docs/user/roadmap.md (scripts/roadmap.py).
# The release each entry belongs to is the issue's milestone on the tracker; this file
#   @theme  release  text          one plain line per release (x.y.z or Later)
#   @word   term  explanation      one line of the "Words on this page" box
#   issue  release  status  changed  text  reason  [short]
#     release  leave empty (if given, it must equal the milestone, or generate fails)
#     status   empty = from the tracker's status/* labels; this column only overrides them
#              (Considering marks an idea not designed yet; its text starts "We are looking at")
#     changed  the version in which a Postponed / Cancelled status was set
#     text     a user-facing UK-English sentence in our own words; '-' hides the issue
#     short    optional label of at most 48 characters for the home page's lane bubble; needed
#              when the text is longer.  The entry's anchor on the page is made from it, so
#              changing it changes the link (keep labels stable)
# Every open type/feature issue in a release up to 1.0 needs a row here (a sentence or '-').
# No Apple marks except to name the hardware, no "Rockbox", no owner media, no jargon.

column3: A new playback engine, one download for every player, and fixes.
Sound and languages: better audio, menus in more languages, better song details, and fixes.
Album art, Album Flow and other screen improvements.
Sleep and battery life, and the first kit for making your own games, with a Sudoku game.
Video: more formats, a better video player, and fixes.
Your library and USB, and the second game kit, with a short role-playing game.
Extras, games and more ways to shape your sound, and the third game kit, with an arcade racing game.
Polish: a careful clean-up of the whole player, making everything as lean and refined as we can, with no new features.
Interoperability Mode, and the last test version before 1.0.
Independence: our own start-up software, Disk Mode, recovery and an installer, so you can fully replace the original software.
Ideas for later, in no fixed order.
the player has two processor cores. Giving the music to the second one keeps the menus smooth on the first.
a separate chip in the player that is good at drawing and handling pictures. Using it takes work off the main processor.
the small program that starts the player before anything else runs (often called a bootloader).
a mode in which the player shows up on your computer as a drive, even when its main software cannot start.
how many times a second the sound is measured, such as 44.1 kHz or 96 kHz.
how finely each of those measurements is stored, such as 16-bit or 24-bit.

column5: MP3 and AAC files use the 24-bit output too, keeping more of their detail.

A new Settings › Audiophile menu with optional 88.2 and 96 kHz output. It is off by default. It runs the audio chip beyond its official range, so it comes with a warning. Your player tests itself first and offers only the rates that pass. If anything goes wrong, it drops back to a safe rate.

column5: The first kit for making your own small games and apps, with a guide. It comes with an original Sudoku game built with the kit.
MPEG-4 videos (up to 320 × 240) play, as well as H.264. These are the two video formats the original player supported.
We are looking at playing MPEG-4 videos larger than 320 × 240.
AVI video files play, when the video inside is a kind the player can decode.
MKV and WebM video files play, once the player can decode the kinds of video they usually hold.
We are looking at playing MPEG-1 and MPEG-2 videos (.mpg files).
We are looking at H.265 (HEVC) video, as an experiment. It ships only if it works well, and is marked experimental if it does.

Subtitles for widescreen videos, from the video file or a .srt file beside it. Turn them on in Videos › Settings.

column5: Interoperability Mode: an optional mode that keeps your library in the format the original software uses, so songs and covers you add with ProkBox5g show up there too. It is off by default, warns you before it changes anything, and offers to back up the original library first.
Our own start-up software, so your player no longer needs the original software at all. It comes only after our own recovery is proven to work.
Our own Disk Mode and recovery: hold a button combination as the player starts, or let it start this way after a failed start, and copy working software back from your computer.

column2: These are things we have decided not to build, each with the reason. It is a list of decisions, not a list of gaps: if the reason changes, we will say so here.

column4: Letting you restyle the player with skins or themes would mean rebuilding that whole system, which is prohibitively difficult when the interface is tuned so closely to the look and behaviour of the original player.
The player always picks the best rate for each file itself, so there is no setting to get wrong. This does not affect the optional high-rate output planned under Audiophile in Settings.
We will not decrypt copy-protected audiobooks or songs, such as Audible files or protected AAC. They show greyed out in your library, and a guide page (planned) explains your options.
Existing plugins will not run here as they are. Games and apps come through our own game kits, which run in a sandbox so a faulty one cannot harm the player.
Settings stays a short, curated list in the original style. Options that change how the player works underneath are not shown.
ProkBox5g is tuned only for the iPod Video (5th generation and 5.5G). Support for other players would be a separate project, not a setting in this firmware.

column5: We are looking at letting the sound chip mute itself during silent stretches, to cut faint hiss in quiet passages and while paused.
Spoken menus: the player can read out menu items and song, artist and album names.
Photos: browse your pictures by album, view them full screen, and play slideshows with music. Copy photos over by drag-and-drop, with no app.
